     1	# VM Resource Instrumentation — Design (rev. 2)
     2	
     3	**Date:** 2026-04-29
     4	**Status:** Design — revised after Codex review (2026-04-29)
     5	**Branch:** `instrumentation`
     6	**Goal:** Give end users live and historical CPU + memory charts for every VM they own.
     7	**Phase 1 scope:** OpenClaw machines only (UI). Browser VM data is collected and stored from day 1, but the browser VM detail page + tab is deferred to Phase 2.
     8	
     9	## Why this matters to users
    10	
    11	When something feels slow inside their VM, the user has no way today to see whether it's CPU-bound, memory-pressured, or just network. They open `/machines/:id` and see static metadata — name, slug, tunnel URL, status — but no signal about how the VM is actually using its 2 vCPU / 2 GB. Rolling out a feature, debugging a hang, or sizing the next VM all benefit from a simple "what's it doing right now" view.
    12	
    13	This design adds a Resources tab on the machine detail page with two sub-views:
    14	
    15	1. **Live** — sliding 5-minute window, refreshing every second, with current-value big numbers above two line charts.
    16	2. **History** — pick a date range, see the full timeline. Available even after a VM is deleted, for the retention window.
    17	
    18	The existing `UsageTab.tsx` already covers token/billing usage. The new tab is **Resources**, not Usage.
    19	
    20	## What gets measured
    21	
    22	For each VM (OpenClaw or Browser):
    23	
    24	- **CPU %** — derived from cgroup `cpu.stat` `usage_usec`, sampled at 1 Hz, computed as `(delta_usage_usec / delta_wall_usec) * 100`. May exceed 100 % for multi-core VMs (correct: a 2-vCPU VM at full load reads 200 %).
    25	- **Memory bytes** — cgroup `memory.current`, sampled at 1 Hz, instantaneous resident.
    26	
    27	Not in this phase: disk I/O, network bytes, page faults, GPU. Easy to add once the pipeline exists.
    28	
    29	## Architecture
    30	
    31	```
    32	                                                              (every 1 s)
    33	[ host: ocm-agent ] ── 1 Hz sample ──▶ in-mem ring (30 s) ──┐
    34	                                                            │ POST every 10 s, batched
    35	                                                            ▼
    36	[ Cloud Run: backend ] ── insert ──▶ vm_metrics_1s (Postgres, daily partitions, ~24 h)
    37	                          │
    38	                          │ 1-min cron downsamples 1 s → 1 m (with watermark + sample_count)
    39	                          ▼
    40	                     vm_metrics_1m (Postgres, daily partitions, 7 d)
    41	                          ▲
    42	[ user browser ] ─────────┴── GET /metrics?from=…&to=…   (history, fetched on view)
    43	                ─────────────  GET /metrics?from=now-5m  (live, polled every 1 s)
    44	```
    45	
    46	**No SSE.** The first revision used Server-Sent Events for the live view. Codex called this out: SSE behind Cloud Run scales with viewers, not VMs (100 open tabs = 100 long-lived handlers + 100 polls/s on Postgres), and the agent batches every 10 s anyway, so per-second SSE frames would be bursty and up to 10 s stale. Replaced with **client-side polling at 1 Hz** — the same backend query path serves both live and history. Live is just a thin convenience: `from = now - 5m, to = now`, polled every second, the chart slides.
    47	
    48	### Source of truth: cgroup v2 on the host
    49	
    50	Every VM already runs in its own systemd unit:
    51	
    52	- `ocm-vm-<machine-id>.service` for OpenClaw VMs
    53	- `ocm-browser-vm-<vm-id>.service` for Browser VMs
    54	
    55	These map to cgroup v2 paths under `/sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/`. The two files we read are kernel-owned and atomic-read:
    56	
    57	- `cpu.stat` — line-oriented; `usage_usec <N>` is the cumulative CPU time charged to the cgroup (microseconds, monotonic *while the cgroup is alive*).
    58	- `memory.current` — single integer, current bytes.
    59	
    60	CPU% formula:
    61	
    62	```
    63	cpu_pct = (cur.usage_usec - prev.usage_usec) / (cur.wall_us - prev.wall_us) * 100
    64	```
    65	
    66	Wall time captured at sample time on the host clock (`time.Now()`), not from any kernel field. This handles the case where two consecutive reads happen 0.97 s and 1.04 s apart — the divisor uses the actual elapsed micros.
    67	
    68	### Discovery and sampler reset semantics
    69	
    70	`cgroup.Discover(root string) []VMRef` scans `system.slice/` every 10 s for entries matching `^ocm-(browser-)?vm-([0-9a-f-]+)\.service$`. Cgroups that disappear between discovery and sample are dropped silently.
    71	
    72	The sampler maintains `prev map[unitName]Sample`. **Reset rules**, all with tests:
    73	
    74	1. On each discovery cycle, prune `prev` entries whose unit no longer exists.
    75	2. On sample, if `cur.usage_usec < prev.usage_usec` (cgroup was destroyed and the unit was reused for a new VM with the same UUID — extremely rare, but possible after stop/start within the discovery window), treat it as a fresh first sample: replace `prev` and emit no point this tick.
    76	3. First sample for a freshly-seen cgroup has no delta → emit a memory-only point with `cpu_pct = NULL`. Schema permits this (see below).
    77	
    78	### Sampling loop (agent)
    79	
    80	New package `backend/internal/vmmetrics/sampler`, single goroutine:
    81	
    82	```go
    83	type Sampler struct {
    84	    Root         string                  // /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice
    85	    Tick         time.Duration           // 1 s
    86	    DiscoverTick time.Duration           // 10 s
    87	    BatchEvery   time.Duration           // 10 s
    88	    HostID       int                     // integer, matches hosts.id
    89	    Pusher       Pusher                  // POST batch to backend
    90	    prev         map[string]Sample
    91	    buffer       []Point                 // ring, capacity ~30 s of samples
    92	}
    93	```
    94	
    95	- 1 Hz tick: for each cgroup, read both files, compute deltas vs `prev`, append a `Point{vm_id, kind, ts, cpu_pct, mem_bytes}` to the buffer (cpu_pct may be null per rule 3).
    96	- Every 10 s: drain buffer into a batch, POST to backend. On non-2xx, requeue with exponential backoff (cap 60 s). On buffer full (>30 s of un-sent data), drop oldest with a counter (`vm_metrics_dropped_total`).
    97	
    98	### Wire format (agent → backend)
    99	
   100	`POST /api/agent/vm-metrics`
   101	
   102	```json
   103	{
   104	  "host_id": 7,
   105	  "points": [
   106	    {
   107	      "vm_id": "9f3c…",
   108	      "kind": "machine",
   109	      "ts": "2026-04-29T18:33:01.000Z",
   110	      "cpu_pct": 12.4,
   111	      "mem_bytes": 524288000
   112	    }
   113	  ]
   114	}
   115	```
   116	
   117	`host_id` is the integer host row id (matches `hosts.id`), encoded as JSON number — same format as heartbeat. `cpu_pct` may be `null` for first samples.
   118	
   119	**Auth (mirrors heartbeat, with one strict difference)** — backend uses the same `authenticateAgent(ctx, r, hostID)` helper at [`backend/internal/api/agent_heartbeat.go:142`](../../backend/internal/api/agent_heartbeat.go), but the metrics handler **rejects the fleet-token fallback**: it requires the per-host token. Reasons:
   120	
   121	- Fleet token grants no host identity (`hostID=0` after auth), so any subsequent placement check is meaningless.
   122	- A leaked fleet token is already a serious incident; we should at minimum prevent it from poisoning every VM's metric stream.
   123	- Hosts always have a per-host token by the time they're sending metrics — heartbeat establishes it. Fleet token is only needed for the very first heartbeat of a new host.
   124	
   125	The handler:
   126	
   127	1. Parses `host_id` as int (mirrors heartbeat).
   128	2. Calls `authenticateAgent(ctx, r, hostID)`. If it returned true via fleet-token fallback (detectable: per-host token didn't exist or didn't match), reject 401.
   129	3. For each point, validates `vm_id` is currently placed on this `host_id`:
   130	   - `kind == "machine"`: `SELECT 1 FROM machines WHERE id = $1 AND host_id = $2 AND deleted_at IS NULL`
   131	   - `kind == "browser"`: `SELECT 1 FROM browser_vms WHERE id = $1 AND host_id = $2`
   132	   - Plus active row in `placements`/`browser_vm_placements` for defense in depth.
   133	4. Looks up `account_id` from the matched VM row and stores it on the metrics row (so reads don't need to join a possibly-deleted VM row).
   134	5. Drops points with `vm_id` that fail validation, returns count in the response (so the agent can log).
   135	
   136	**Ingest validation, all enforced server-side, all tested:**
   137	
   138	- `Content-Length` ≤ 64 KiB.
   139	- `points` length ≤ 1000.
   140	- For each point: `ts` within ±5 min of server time; `mem_bytes ≥ 0`; `cpu_pct` either null or in `[0, 100 * vcpus * 2]` (vcpus from VM row; the *2 is slack for noisy kernel accounting).
   141	- All `ts` rounded to second-precision (nanos discarded).
   142	- Future-dated points (which would auto-create future partitions on insert) are rejected before reaching the DB.
   143	
   144	### Storage schema
   145	
   146	Migration `084_vm_metrics.sql`. Two tables, partitioned by day on `ts`:
   147	
   148	```sql
   149	CREATE TABLE vm_metrics_1s (
   150	    account_id INT          NOT NULL,
   151	    host_id    INT          NOT NULL,
   152	    vm_id      UUID         NOT NULL,
   153	    kind       TEXT         NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('machine', 'browser')),
   154	    ts         TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL,
   155	    cpu_pct    REAL,                                -- NULL allowed for first sample
   156	    mem_bytes  BIGINT       NOT NULL CHECK (mem_bytes >= 0),
   157	    PRIMARY KEY (vm_id, kind, ts)
   158	) PARTITION BY RANGE (ts);
   159	
   160	-- Access path is "give me points for one VM in this account in this time range",
   161	-- and "list all my account's VMs over a range" for any future fleet view.
   162	CREATE INDEX vm_metrics_1s_account_vm_ts ON vm_metrics_1s (account_id, vm_id, kind, ts);
   163	
   164	CREATE TABLE vm_metrics_1m (
   165	    account_id   INT          NOT NULL,
   166	    host_id      INT          NOT NULL,           -- last host the bucket saw; informational
   167	    vm_id        UUID         NOT NULL,
   168	    kind         TEXT         NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('machine', 'browser')),
   169	    ts           TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL,           -- minute-aligned bucket start
   170	    cpu_pct      REAL,                            -- avg over the minute, NULL if no samples had cpu_pct
   171	    mem_bytes    BIGINT       NOT NULL CHECK (mem_bytes >= 0),
   172	    sample_count INT          NOT NULL,           -- how many 1s rows fed this bucket
   173	    finalized    BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
   174	    PRIMARY KEY (vm_id, kind, ts)
   175	) PARTITION BY RANGE (ts);
   176	
   177	CREATE INDEX vm_metrics_1m_account_vm_ts ON vm_metrics_1m (account_id, vm_id, kind, ts);
   178	```
   179	
   180	No FK to `machines.id` or `browser_vms.id` — metrics outlive the VM row. `account_id` is denormalized so deleted-VM history reads still authorize cleanly. (Codex CRITICAL.)
   181	
   182	PK includes `kind` because a UUID collision across tables, while astronomically unlikely, isn't structurally impossible; a check constraint costs nothing and keeps the model honest.
   183	
   184	Daily partitions named `vm_metrics_1s_y2026m04d29`. **Retention is daily-granular**, not exactly 24 h or 7 d — a partition can survive up to 24 h past the nominal cutoff before the cron drops it. Acceptable for Phase 1 and explicitly documented.
   185	
   186	### Maintenance crons (singleton via pg advisory locks)
   187	
   188	A new package `backend/internal/vmmetrics/maint` exposes three jobs. Cloud Run runs N instances; each starts the loops, but each job acquires a pg advisory lock before running. Constants live in `maint/locks.go`:
   189	
   190	```go
   191	const (
   192	    lockEnsurePartitions int64 = 0x564D5F455053 // "VM_EPS"
   193	    lockDownsample1s1m   int64 = 0x564D5F4453   // "VM_DS"
   194	    lockDropPartitions   int64 = 0x564D5F4452   // "VM_DR"
   195	)
   196	```
   197	
   198	Each job:
   199	
   200	```go
   201	func runWithLock(ctx, db, key int64, job func(...)) {
   202	    ok, _ := db.AcquireAdvisory(ctx, key)
   203	    if !ok { return }
   204	    defer db.ReleaseAdvisory(ctx, key)
   205	    job(...)
   206	}
   207	```
   208	
   209	| Job | Frequency | What it does |
   210	|-----|-----------|--------------|
   211	| `EnsurePartitions` | every 1 h | Create partitions for `today + 0..3` days for both tables. Idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS`). |
   212	| `Downsample1s1m` | every 1 min | For each `(vm_id, kind, minute_bucket)` whose bucket end is older than the **watermark** (currently `now() - 90s`, > max retry window) and not yet `finalized`: aggregate matching 1 s rows, upsert into `vm_metrics_1m` with `sample_count = N`, set `finalized = true` only if `N >= 60` *or* `bucket_end < now() - 5min` (give very-late points a few minutes to land). |
   213	| `DropOldPartitions` | every 1 h | `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` 1 s partitions whose nominal date is more than 1 day before today (UTC), 1 m partitions more than 7 days before. |
   214	
   215	**Late-arrival handling (Codex IMPORTANT):** The first revision used `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, which freezes a partial bucket if more samples land later. Now: `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (vm_id, kind, ts) DO UPDATE SET cpu_pct = EXCLUDED.cpu_pct, mem_bytes = EXCLUDED.mem_bytes, sample_count = EXCLUDED.sample_count, host_id = EXCLUDED.host_id WHERE NOT vm_metrics_1m.finalized`. Once a bucket is finalized (5 min past close), late points are silently discarded.
   216	
   217	Insert path failure if today's partition is missing: `EnsurePartitions` runs at `t-0` boot and every hour. If a point lands and the partition isn't there yet, the insert fails with a clear error → the agent batch retries → typically next batch (10 s later) succeeds because the next maintenance tick (or boot run) created it. Tested.
   218	
   219	### User-facing endpoints (account-scoped, matches existing convention)
   220	
   221	All under `/api/accounts/{accountId}/...`, all pass through `srv.AccountMiddleware` for membership auth (matches `backend/internal/api/server.go:362-405`).
   222	
   223	#### Phase 1 — machines only
   224	
   225	```
   226	GET /api/accounts/{accountId}/machines/{id}/metrics?from=<ISO>&to=<ISO>
   227	```
   228	
   229	Server picks resolution by range:
   230	
   231	- `to - from <= 1h` → query `vm_metrics_1s`
   232	- `to - from > 1h` → query `vm_metrics_1m`
   233	
   234	If a range straddles the 1 s retention boundary (e.g., `from = -25h, to = now`), the server splits the query: 1 m for the older portion, 1 s for the last 24 h. The response carries `resolution: "1s" | "1m" | "mixed"`.
   235	
   236	Hard cap: `to - from <= 7d`. Larger ranges → 400.
   237	
   238	Response:
   239	
   240	```json
   241	{
   242	  "vm_id": "…",
   243	  "resolution": "1s",
   244	  "from": "…",
   245	  "to": "…",
   246	  "points": [{"ts": "…", "cpu_pct": 12.4, "mem_bytes": 524288000}]
   247	}
   248	```
   249	
   250	Live view is just `from = now - 5m`, polled every 1 s by the frontend. Server doesn't need to know "live" vs "history".
   251	
   252	Authorization: the handler verifies the machine belongs to `accountId`. For deleted machines, the metrics rows still carry `account_id`, and the same handler returns history if the caller's account matches that stored `account_id`. Tested.
   253	
   254	#### Phase 1 — browser VMs (data only, no UI)
   255	
   256	```
   257	GET /api/accounts/{accountId}/browser-vms/{id}/metrics?from=<ISO>&to=<ISO>
   258	```
   259	
   260	Same shape as machines, gated on browser-VM ownership. No frontend in Phase 1 — Codex correctly noted that `BrowserVMLivePage` is an iframe proxy, not a tabbed detail page, so a browser-VM detail UI is its own design (Phase 2).

   168	   131	## Test-Driven Feature Development
   169	   132	
   170	   133	When implementing a new feature, follow this workflow strictly. Do NOT skip steps. Do NOT mark items complete without test proof.
   171	   134	
   172	   135	1. **CLARIFY**: Before writing any code, summarize back in 3-4 bullet points what is being asked for. Include the user-facing behavior, not infrastructure details. Wait for approval.
   173	   136	2. **TEST FIRST**: Write integration/unit tests that define the acceptance criteria. For Go code use table-driven tests. For TypeScript use the existing test framework. Tests should cover happy path, error cases, and edge cases.
   174	   137	3. **RUN TESTS (they should all fail)**: Execute the test suite and confirm everything fails for the right reasons.
   175	   138	4. **IMPLEMENT**: Write the minimal code to make tests pass. After each significant change, run the full test suite.
   176	   139	5. **ITERATE**: Keep running tests and fixing until ALL pass. Do not claim something works without showing green test output.
   177	   140	6. **VERIFY**: Run `grep -r` for any TODO/FIXME introduced. Check for hardcoded values that should be config. Run the linter.

   230	   193	- No unused locals or parameters (`noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`)

   237	   200	
   238	   201	## Architecture Reference
   239	   202	
   240	   203	Split-plane architecture (from ClaraTeach):
   241	   204	- **Control Plane** — stateless Go API on Cloud Run (port 8080)
   242	   205	- **Worker Agents** — Go process on GCP Compute VMs (ports 9090/9091), manages Firecracker MicroVMs
   243	   206	- **Each OpenClaw instance** = one Firecracker MicroVM (~125ms boot, KVM isolation)
   244	   207	- **Networking** via Cloudflare Tunnel
   245	   208	
   246	   209	See `docs/architecture.md` for full details.
   247	   210	
   248	   211	### Configuration Pipeline
   249	   212	
   250	   213	`configassembly` package assembles gateway config from three layers: platform defaults → user config (pushed via API) → credential injection. The assembled config is served to VMs via the metadata server.
   251	   214	
   252	   215	## Artifact Delivery Chain
   253	   216	
   254	   217	GCS bucket → `manifest.json` → Cloud Run env var → provisioner → GCE instance metadata → agent reads metadata → downloads artifact.
   255	   218	
   256	   219	- **Rootfs and OpenClaw artifacts are decoupled from the agent.** New VMs pull the latest versions from GCS at start time. No agent restart is needed for rootfs or openclaw changes.
   257	   220	- **Agent updates are manual.** After `make upload-agent`, hosts stay on their current version until an admin clicks the "Update" button on the AdminHosts page (one host at a time). The update restarts the agent via systemd; Firecracker VMs survive because the default runtime-owner is `systemd-unit` (each VM runs in its own per-VM unit, `ocm-vm-<id>.service` / `ocm-browser-vm-<id>.service`, independent of `ocm-agent.service`). `KillMode=process` on the agent unit further guards legacy direct-owner VMs from the cgroup SIGKILL. See `docs/plans/2026-04-11-vm-runtime-ownership-split.md`. Fresh hosts still pull the latest agent at first boot; only steady-state updates require the manual click. Only upload a new agent (`make upload-agent`) when agent code actually changed.
   258	   221	- After `make build-upload-rootfs`, new VMs immediately get the new rootfs. Existing running VMs are unaffected.
   259	   222	- To check agent logs: `gcloud compute ssh <VM> --zone=<ZONE> --command="sudo journalctl -u ocm-agent --since '30 min ago' | grep -i selfupdate"`

   279	### Naming and FK awareness
   280	
   281	`kind` discriminator avoids ambiguity. UUIDs are unique-per-table in practice but the discriminator costs ~1 byte and keeps queries explicit. The user-facing endpoints take a path-typed id and *know* the kind, so they always filter on `(account_id, kind, vm_id)` together.

   283	## Test plan (additions in **bold** are from the Codex review)
   284	
   285	### Backend unit (Go)
   286	
   287	- `cgroup.ParseCPUStat` — fixture text parses; missing `usage_usec` field returns error.
   288	- `cgroup.ParseMemoryCurrent` — single-integer file parses; whitespace tolerated.
   289	- `cgroup.CPUPercent(prev, curr)` — known deltas → known %, including >100 %, divide-by-zero → 0, **and the `cur < prev` reset case → returns "first sample" sentinel**.
   290	- `cgroup.Discover(root)` — fixture dir with mixed `ocm-vm-*`, `ocm-browser-vm-*`, `unrelated.service` → only VM units returned, kind classified correctly.
   291	- `sampler.Tick` — fed two synthetic samples → one point with the expected fields. **First sample emits null cpu_pct.** **Cgroup-disappear pruning: stop the cgroup, run discover, ensure prev entry is removed.**
   292	- `store.InsertVMMetrics` (integration, real Postgres via testcontainers) — round-trips a 200-point batch. **Null cpu_pct round-trips correctly.**
   293	- `store.QueryVMMetrics` — given seeded data, returns the right slice for a range; resolution selection picks `_1s` for ≤1h, `_1m` for >1h, `mixed` for straddle ranges.
   294	- **`store.QueryVMMetricsForDeletedMachine`** — seed metrics with `account_id`, delete the `machines` row, query as the owning account → still returns history.
   295	- **`store.AccountIDFromMetrics`** — denormalized `account_id` enforces ownership without joining the live VM row.
   296	- `maint.Downsample1s1m` — seed 60 1 s points across one minute, run, expect one 1 m row with correct avg + `sample_count = 60` + `finalized = true`. Run again → no-op.
   297	- **`maint.Downsample1s1m` late-arrival** — seed 30 of 60 points, run after 90 s → unfinalized 1 m row with `sample_count = 30`. Add the other 30 within the finalization window → re-run → updated row with `sample_count = 60`, `finalized = true`. Add a point after finalization → silently dropped.
   298	- `maint.DropOldPartitions` — seed daily partitions for the last 30 days → 1 s partitions older than 1 day and 1 m partitions older than 7 days dropped. **UTC midnight rollover: simulate two runs straddling 23:59:30 → 00:00:30, no partition is dropped that the next minute would still write to.**
   299	- `maint.EnsurePartitions` — fresh DB → today + 3 future partitions exist on both tables.
   300	- **`maint.AdvisoryLockContention`** — start two `Downsample1s1m` jobs concurrently against the same DB; only one runs at a time, second exits cleanly.
   301	- **`Insert with no partition`** — drop today's partition, insert a point → fails with the expected SQLSTATE; agent retry behavior tested in the HTTP layer.
   302	
   303	### Backend HTTP (Go)
   304	
   305	- `POST /api/agent/vm-metrics` — bearer-auth: missing token 401, wrong token 401, **fleet-token 401 (must be per-host)**, valid → 204 + rows in DB.
   306	- `POST` — point with wrong `host_id` for the `vm_id` is rejected (count returned in response).
   307	- **`POST` validation**: oversize body 413; >1000 points 400; ts older than 5 min skew 400; ts in the future 400; negative `mem_bytes` 400; `cpu_pct` outside `[0, 100*vcpus*2]` 400.
   308	- **`POST` duplicate semantics**: same (vm_id, kind, ts) twice in one batch → second is dropped, response counts mismatch.
   309	- `GET …/machines/:id/metrics` — owner gets points; non-owner gets 403; **deleted-VM range still returns historical points to the owning account; cross-account access still 403.**
   310	- `GET …/machines/:id/metrics?from=…&to=…` — straddle range returns `resolution: "mixed"` and merged points.

   343	## Risks and open questions
   344	
   345	- **Cardinality at 1 Hz**: 100 concurrent VMs → 8.6 M rows/day in `vm_metrics_1s`, ~430 MB before pg overhead. Daily partitions cap query scan to one day. If write rate becomes a problem we can drop tick to 2 s or push aggregates from agent.
   346	- **Polling at 1 Hz**: 100 simultaneously-open Resources tabs = 100 indexed reads/s, each scanning ~5 minutes of 1 s data for one VM (= ~300 rows). Trivial. We accept up to 10 s data freshness because the agent batches every 10 s — the live chart visibly lags real-time by that much, which is honest and matches the data we actually have.
   347	- **VM moves between hosts**: each batch is host-scoped. If a VM moves, the new host's agent picks up its cgroup and continues sampling. The 1 s history just has a few-second gap during the move.
   348	- **Legacy direct-owner VMs (pre runtime-ownership-split)**: their cgroup isn't `system.slice/ocm-vm-*.service`. Sampler won't see them. Acceptable — those are being migrated out anyway.
   349	- **Privacy**: CPU/memory of one user's VM is not visible to others — strictly account-scoped at the API layer. The agent → backend ingest doesn't carry user identity at all; ownership is resolved server-side via host placement and stored on the metric row.
   350	- **Browser VM UI**: deferred to Phase 2 along with the broader question of what a browser-VM detail page should look like. Phase 1 collects and stores browser-VM metrics from day 1 so Phase 2 starts with data, not a backfill.
   351	- **Storage growth past Phase 1**: at 1 m × 7 d × 100 VMs = 1 M rows in `vm_metrics_1m`. Fine. Disk and network would add columns or sibling tables; design accommodates either.
   352	- **Retention is daily-granular, not exact**: dropping whole partitions means a 1 s row can live up to ~48 h before its partition is dropped. Acceptable Phase 1; if exact retention matters later, switch to row-level deletes or hourly partitions.
   353	
   354	## Out of scope (Phase 2+)
   355	
   356	- Browser VM detail page + Resources tab.
   357	- Disk I/O, network counters, page faults — same pipeline, more cgroup fields.
   358	- Alerting ("ping me if my VM is at 95 % CPU for 5 min").
   359	- Aggregated views (account-wide rollup, host-wide rollup).
   360	- Export to Prometheus / OpenTelemetry — straightforward once the schema is stable.

   260	   223	
   261	   224	## Init Script Environment Scoping (`scripts/init-openclaw.sh`)
   262	   225	
   263	   226	The init script has **three separate environment contexts**. Env vars needed by multiple contexts must be added to each:
   264	   227	
   265	   228	1. **Gateway env block** (`su -s /bin/bash openclaw -c "..."` starting the gateway) — has `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, `OCM_CONFIG_SOURCE`, etc.
   266	   229	2. **PTY server env block** (`su -s /bin/bash openclaw -c "..."` starting `agent --pty-server`) — spawned commands (`openclaw tui`, `tail -f`) inherit this env, NOT shell profile
   267	   230	3. **`/etc/profile.d/` scripts** — only sourced by login shells (`/bin/bash --login`), not direct command execution
   268	   231	
   269	   232	## Firecracker VM Environment
   270	   233	
   271	   234	- Minimal `/dev` — no udev, no `/dev/fd` symlink by default
   272	   235	- Process substitution `>(tee ...)` needs `/dev/fd → /proc/self/fd` symlink created explicitly
   273	   236	- Must `mount -t proc proc /proc` before `/dev/fd` symlink works
   274	   237	- Init script is PID 1 — no systemd, no services, everything is manual
   275	   238	- Gateway startup takes ~55s (Node.js module loading) — quick-start only skips sidecars
   276	   239	
   277	   240	## Common Fixes
   278	   241	
   279	   242	| Problem | Solution |
   280	   243	|---------|----------|
   281	   244	| Stale deployment | `make deploy-all` |
   282	   245	| Agent not updating | `make upload-agent` (uploads to GCS), then click "Update" on the host row in AdminHosts. No polling — hosts do not auto-update. The agent restart is in-place; Firecracker VMs keep running under their per-VM systemd units. |
   283	   246	| Rootfs stale on new VMs | `make build-upload-rootfs` — new VMs pull immediately from GCS, no agent restart needed |
   284	   247	| VM not provisioning | Check GCP Console VM logs |

   295	 succeeded in 0ms:
   296	     1	# VM Resource Instrumentation — Design
   297	     2	
   298	     3	**Date:** 2026-04-29
   299	     4	**Status:** Design — pending Codex review
   300	     5	**Branch:** `instrumentation`
   301	     6	**Goal:** Give end users live and historical CPU + memory charts for every VM they own (OpenClaw + Browser).
   302	     7	
   303	     8	## Why this matters to users
   304	     9	
   305	    10	When something feels slow inside their VM, the user has no way today to see whether it's CPU-bound, memory-pressured, or just network. They open `/machines/:id` and see static metadata — name, slug, tunnel URL, status — but no signal about how the VM is actually using its 2 vCPU / 2 GB. Rolling out a feature, debugging a hang, or sizing the next VM all benefit from a simple "what's it doing right now" view.
   306	    11	
   307	    12	This design adds a Resources tab on the machine detail page (and the equivalent for browser VMs) with two sub-views:
   308	    13	
   309	    14	1. **Live** — sliding 5-minute window, refreshing every second, with current-value big numbers above two line charts.
   310	    15	2. **History** — pick a date range, see the full timeline, zoom and pan. Available even after a VM stops, for the retention window.
   311	    16	
   312	    17	Naming note: the existing `UsageTab.tsx` already covers token/billing usage. The new tab is **Resources**, not Usage, to avoid collision.
   313	    18	
   314	    19	## What gets measured
   315	    20	
   316	    21	For each VM (OpenClaw or Browser):
   317	    22	
   318	    23	- **CPU %** — derived from cgroup `cpu.stat` `usage_usec`, sampled at 1 Hz, computed as `(delta_usage_usec / delta_wall_usec) * 100`. May exceed 100 % for multi-core VMs (correct: a 2-vCPU VM at full load reads 200 %).
   319	    24	- **Memory bytes** — cgroup `memory.current`, sampled at 1 Hz, instantaneous resident.
   320	    25	
   321	    26	Not in this phase: disk I/O, network bytes, page faults, GPU. Easy to add once the pipeline exists.
   322	    27	
   323	    28	## Architecture
   324	    29	
   325	    30	```
   326	    31	                                                                 (every 1 s)
   327	    32	[ host: ocm-agent ] ── 1 Hz sample ──▶ in-mem ring (30 s) ──┐
   328	    33	                                                            │ POST every 10 s, batched
   329	    34	                                                            ▼
   330	    35	[ Cloud Run: backend ] ── insert ──▶ vm_metrics_1s (Postgres, daily partitions, 24 h)
   331	    36	                          │
   332	    37	                          │ minute-cron downsamples 1 s → 1 m
   333	    38	                          ▼
   334	    39	                     vm_metrics_1m (Postgres, daily partitions, 7 d)
   335	    40	                          ▲
   336	    41	[ user browser ] ─────────┴── GET /metrics?from=…&to=… (history)
   337	    42	                ─────────────  GET /metrics/live (SSE, 1 s frames)
   338	    43	```
   339	    44	
   340	    45	### Source of truth: cgroup v2 on the host
   341	    46	
   342	    47	Every VM already runs in its own systemd unit:
   343	    48	
   344	    49	- `ocm-vm-<machine-id>.service` for OpenClaw VMs
   345	    50	- `ocm-browser-vm-<vm-id>.service` for Browser VMs
   346	    51	
   347	    52	These map to cgroup v2 paths under `/sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/`. The two files we read are stable, kernel-owned, atomic-read:
   348	    53	
   349	    54	- `cpu.stat` — line-oriented, `usage_usec <N>` is the cumulative CPU time charged to the cgroup (microseconds, monotonic).
   350	    55	- `memory.current` — single integer, current bytes.
   351	    56	
   352	    57	CPU% formula:
   353	    58	
   354	    59	```
   355	    60	cpu_pct = (cur.usage_usec - prev.usage_usec) / (cur.wall_ns / 1000 - prev.wall_ns / 1000) * 100
   356	    61	```
   357	    62	
   358	    63	Wall time is captured at sample time on the host clock (`time.Now()`), not from any kernel field. This handles the case where two consecutive reads happen 0.97 s and 1.04 s apart — the divisor uses the actual elapsed micros, not a hardcoded 1_000_000.
   359	    64	
   360	    65	### Discovery
   361	    66	
   362	    67	A `cgroup.Discover(root string) []VMRef` function scans `system.slice/` for entries matching `^ocm-(browser-)?vm-([0-9a-f-]+)\.service$`. It extracts the kind (`machine` vs `browser`) and the VM UUID. Cgroups that disappear between discovery and sample (because the VM stopped mid-tick) are dropped silently.
   363	    68	
   364	    69	Discovery runs every 10 s, not every 1 s — the cgroup set rarely changes.
   365	    70	
   366	    71	### Sampling loop (agent)
   367	    72	
   368	    73	A new package `backend/internal/vmmetrics/sampler` owns a single goroutine:
   369	    74	
   370	    75	```go
   371	    76	type Sampler struct {
   372	    77	    Root       string                  // /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice
   373	    78	    Tick       time.Duration           // 1 * time.Second
   374	    79	    BatchEvery time.Duration           // 10 * time.Second
   375	    80	    HostID     string
   376	    81	    Pusher     Pusher                  // POST batch to backend
   377	    82	    prev       map[string]Sample       // last sample per cgroup-name
   378	    83	    buffer     []Point                 // ring, capacity 30s * #vms
   379	    84	}
   380	    85	```
   381	    86	
   382	    87	- 1 Hz tick: for each cgroup, read both files, compute deltas vs `prev`, append a `Point{vm_id, kind, ts, cpu_pct, mem_bytes}` to the buffer.
   383	    88	- Every 10 s, drain the buffer into a batch, POST to backend. On non-2xx, requeue with exponential backoff (cap 60 s). On buffer full (>30 s of data unsent), drop oldest with a counter incremented (`vm_metrics_dropped_total`).
   384	    89	- First sample for a new cgroup has no `prev`, so cpu_pct is omitted; memory is reported. Second tick produces the first cpu_pct.
   385	    90	
   386	    91	### Wire format (agent → backend)
   387	    92	
   388	    93	`POST /api/v1/agent/vm-metrics`
   389	    94	
   390	    95	```json
   391	    96	{
   392	    97	  "host_id": "h-east-3",
   393	    98	  "points": [
   394	    99	    {
   395	   100	      "vm_id": "9f3c…",
   396	   101	      "kind": "machine",
   397	   102	      "ts": "2026-04-29T18:33:01.000Z",
   398	   103	      "cpu_pct": 12.4,
   399	   104	      "mem_bytes": 524288000
   400	   105	    },
   401	   106	    …up to ~200 points per host…
   402	   107	  ]
   403	   108	}
   404	   109	```
   405	   110	
   406	   111	Auth: same Bearer token the agent already sends for heartbeat (`AgentToken`), validated against the host row's stored token. Backend rejects points whose `vm_id` is not currently placed on this host (defense against a compromised agent injecting metrics for VMs it doesn't own).
   407	   112	
   408	   113	`kind` is `"machine"` or `"browser"`. The two VM tables (`machines` / `browser_vms`) live in different namespaces, so the discriminator is needed for FK validation and routing.
   409	   114	
   410	   115	### Storage schema
   411	   116	
   412	   117	Two tables, each partitioned by day on `ts`. New migration: `084_vm_metrics.sql`.
   413	   118	
   414	   119	```sql
   415	   120	CREATE TABLE vm_metrics_1s (
   416	   121	    vm_id      UUID         NOT NULL,
   417	   122	    kind       TEXT         NOT NULL,   -- 'machine' | 'browser'
   418	   123	    ts         TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL,
   419	   124	    cpu_pct    REAL         NOT NULL,
   420	   125	    mem_bytes  BIGINT       NOT NULL,
   421	   126	    PRIMARY KEY (vm_id, ts)
   422	   127	) PARTITION BY RANGE (ts);
   423	   128	
   424	   129	CREATE INDEX vm_metrics_1s_kind_ts ON vm_metrics_1s (kind, ts);
   425	   130	
   426	   131	CREATE TABLE vm_metrics_1m (
   427	   132	    vm_id      UUID         NOT NULL,
   428	   133	    kind       TEXT         NOT NULL,
   429	   134	    ts         TIMESTAMPTZ  NOT NULL,    -- bucket start, minute-aligned
   430	   135	    cpu_pct    REAL         NOT NULL,    -- avg over the minute
   431	   136	    mem_bytes  BIGINT       NOT NULL,    -- avg over the minute
   432	   137	    PRIMARY KEY (vm_id, ts)
   433	   138	) PARTITION BY RANGE (ts);
   434	   139	```
   435	   140	
   436	   141	No FK to `machines.id` or `browser_vms.id` — the metrics outlive the VMs (history view should still work after a VM is deleted, until retention drops it).
   437	   142	
   438	   143	Daily partitions named `vm_metrics_1s_y2026m04d29`. A maintenance cron creates the next 3 days of partitions ahead of time and drops partitions older than retention.
   439	   144	
   440	   145	### Cron jobs (backend)
   441	   146	
   442	   147	A new package `backend/internal/vmmetrics/maint` exposes three jobs that the existing fleet scheduler invokes:
   443	   148	
   444	   149	| Job | Frequency | What it does |
   445	   150	|-----|-----------|--------------|
   446	   151	| `EnsurePartitions` | every 1 h | Create partitions for `today + 0..3` days for both tables. Idempotent. |
   447	   152	| `Downsample1s1m` | every 1 min | Insert 1-min buckets for the 1 s rows from `now() - 65s` to `now() - 5s` that aren't already in `vm_metrics_1m`. `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. |
   448	   153	| `DropOldPartitions` | every 1 h | `DROP TABLE` 1 s partitions older than 24 h, 1 m partitions older than 7 d. |
   449	   154	
   450	   155	The 65 s / 5 s window for downsample tolerates clock skew and late-arriving batches. Once a minute-bucket exists in `vm_metrics_1m`, it's never updated — late points within the bucket are discarded. Acceptable: the drop is bounded by batch size (10 s) so the worst-case error in a 60 s avg is one data point.
   451	   156	
   452	   157	### User-facing endpoints
   453	   158	
   454	   159	All three endpoints check that the caller's account owns the VM. 403 on mismatch.
   455	   160	
   456	   161	#### History
   457	   162	
   458	   163	```
   459	   164	GET /api/v1/machines/:id/metrics?from=<ISO>&to=<ISO>
   460	   165	GET /api/v1/browser-vms/:id/metrics?from=<ISO>&to=<ISO>
   461	   166	```
   462	   167	
   463	   168	Server picks resolution by range:
   464	   169	
   465	   170	- `to - from <= 1h` → query `vm_metrics_1s`
   466	   171	- `to - from > 1h` → query `vm_metrics_1m`
   467	   172	
   468	   173	If a range straddles the 1 s retention boundary (e.g., `from = -25h, to = now`), the server splits the query: 1 m for the older portion, 1 s for the last 24 h. The response carries `resolution: "1s" | "1m" | "mixed"`.
   469	   174	
   470	   175	Hard cap: `to - from <= 7d` (the longer-retention window). Larger ranges return 400.
   471	   176	
   472	   177	Response:
   473	   178	
   474	   179	```json
   475	   180	{
   476	   181	  "vm_id": "…",
   477	   182	  "resolution": "1s",
   478	   183	  "from": "…",
   479	   184	  "to": "…",
   480	   185	  "points": [{"ts": "…", "cpu_pct": 12.4, "mem_bytes": 524288000}, …]
   481	   186	}
   482	   187	```
   483	   188	
   484	   189	#### Live (SSE)
   485	   190	
   486	   191	```
   487	   192	GET /api/v1/machines/:id/metrics/live
   488	   193	GET /api/v1/browser-vms/:id/metrics/live
   489	   194	```
   490	   195	
   491	   196	Server-Sent Events stream. On open, the server emits the last 5 minutes of 1 s data immediately as one event, then continues to emit one event per second as new data lands.
   492	   197	
   493	   198	Implementation: backend tails `vm_metrics_1s` with a 1 s polling query (`WHERE vm_id = $1 AND ts > $2 ORDER BY ts`). Cheap because the index covers it and the per-second batch from agents lands within ~10 s.
   494	   199	
   495	   200	We deliberately do **not** ask the agent to push directly to the user — too many edge cases (auth, NAT, agent restarts). Pushing through the backend keeps a single auth surface and lets the user disconnect/reconnect cheaply.
   496	   201	
   497	   202	### Frontend
   498	   203	
   499	   204	New tab `ResourcesTab.tsx` registered in `MachineView.tsx` and `BrowserVMLivePage.tsx`. Two sub-tabs (regular Radix `<Tabs>`):
   500	   205	
   501	   206	- **Live** (default)
   502	   207	  - Two big-number readouts at the top: "CPU 14.2 %", "Memory 512 MB / 2 GB" (memory shows total from the VM's `memory_mb` field).
   503	   208	  - Two stacked Recharts `<LineChart>` components, 5-minute window.
   504	   209	  - SSE `EventSource` connection. Buffers points client-side, drops anything older than 5 min on each tick.
   505	   210	- **History**
   506	   211	  - Date+time range picker (default: last 24 h).
   507	   212	  - Single `<LineChart>` per metric, full range.
   508	   213	  - Resolution badge: "1-second" or "1-minute".
   509	   214	  - Wheel-zoom + drag-pan (Recharts `Brush` component is a simpler first cut).
   510	   215	
   511	   216	Add `recharts` to `frontend/package.json`. No other frontend deps.
   512	   217	
   513	   218	### Naming and FK awareness
   514	   219	
   515	   220	The `kind` column avoids ambiguity at query time. The user-facing endpoints take a `vm_id` and *know* whether they're hitting `/machines/:id` or `/browser-vms/:id`, so they always filter `kind = 'machine'` or `kind = 'browser'` along with `vm_id` for safety, even though the UUID alone is unique across both tables in practice.
   516	   221

   519	   224	### Backend unit (Go)
   520	   225	
   521	   226	- `cgroup.ParseCPUStat` — fixture text parses correctly, missing `usage_usec` field returns error.

   525	   230	- `sampler.Tick` — fed two synthetic samples, produces one point with the expected fields.
   526	   231	- `store.InsertVMMetrics` (integration, real Postgres via testcontainers) — round-trips a 200-point batch.
   527	   232	- `store.QueryVMMetrics` — given seeded data, returns the right slice for a range; resolution selection picks `_1s` for ≤1h, `_1m` for >1h.
   528	   233	- `maint.Downsample1s1m` — seed 60 1 s points across one minute, run, expect one 1 m row with the correct avg. Run again — no-op (idempotent).
   529	   234	- `maint.DropOldPartitions` — seed daily partitions for last 30 days, run, expect 1 s partitions older than 1 day and 1 m partitions older than 7 days dropped.
   530	   235	- `maint.EnsurePartitions` — fresh DB, run, expect today + 3 future partitions to exist on both tables.

   563	   268	5. **Backend ingest endpoint** — `POST /api/v1/agent/vm-metrics` with auth + placement check.
   564	   269	6. **Maintenance crons** — `EnsurePartitions`, `Downsample1s1m`, `DropOldPartitions` wired into the fleet scheduler.
   565	   270	7. **User history endpoint** — `GET /machines/:id/metrics` + `GET /browser-vms/:id/metrics`.

   569	   274	
   570	   275	## Risks and open questions
   571	   276	
   572	   277	- **Cardinality at 1 Hz**: 100 concurrent VMs → 8.6 M rows/day in `vm_metrics_1s`, ~430 MB before pg overhead. Daily partitions cap query scan to one day. If write rate becomes a problem we can reduce the tick to 2 s or push aggregates from agent.
   573	   278	- **SSE through Cloud Run**: Cloud Run terminates idle connections after 60 min. SSE handler emits a heartbeat comment every 30 s to keep the proxy from buffering, and the client transparently reconnects on EOF.
   574	   279	- **VM moves between hosts**: each batch is host-scoped. If a VM moves, the new host's agent picks up its cgroup and continues sampling — no special handling. The 1 s history just has a few-second gap during the move.
   575	   280	- **Legacy direct-owner VMs (pre runtime-ownership-split)**: their cgroup isn't `system.slice/ocm-vm-*.service`. Sampler won't see them. Acceptable — those are being migrated out anyway, and this feature is explicitly forward-looking.
   576	   281	- **Privacy**: CPU/memory of one user's VM is not visible to others — strictly account-scoped at the API layer. The agent → backend ingest doesn't carry user identity at all; ownership is resolved server-side via host placement.
   577	   282	- **Storage growth past Phase 1**: at 1 m × 7 d × 50 VMs = 0.5 M rows total in `vm_metrics_1m`. Fine. If we later add disk and network we'd add columns or tables; design accommodates either.
   578	   283	
   579	   284	## Out of scope (Phase 2+)
   580	   285	
   581	   286	- Disk I/O, network counters, page faults — same pipeline, more cgroup fields.
   582	   287	- Alerting ("ping me if my VM is at 95 % CPU for 5 min").
   583	   288	- Aggregated views (account-wide rollup, host-wide rollup).
   584	   289	- Export to Prometheus / OpenTelemetry — straightforward once the schema is stable.

    22	func (s *Server) reconcileHostBrowserPairings(ctx context.Context, host *store.Host) {
    23		if s.agentClient == nil || host == nil {
    24			return
    25		}
    26	
    27		machines, err := s.store.ListMachinesByHost(ctx, host.ID)
    28		if err != nil {
    29			slog.Warn("heartbeat.browser_pairings.list_machines_failed", "host_id", host.ID, "error", err)
    30			return
    31		}
    32	
    33		for _, machine := range machines {
    34			if machine.Status != "running" || machine.BrowserVMID == nil || machine.VMIP == nil {
    35				continue
    36			}
    37	
    38			bvm, err := s.store.GetBrowserVM(ctx, *machine.BrowserVMID)
    39			if err != nil {
    40				slog.Warn("heartbeat.browser_pairings.get_browser_vm_failed",
    41					"host_id", host.ID,
    42					"machine_id", machine.ID,
    43					"browser_vm_id", *machine.BrowserVMID,
    44					"error", err)
    45				continue
    46			}
    47			if bvm == nil || bvm.Status != "running" || bvm.VMIP == nil || bvm.HostID == nil || *bvm.HostID != host.ID {
    48				continue
    49			}
    50	
    51			if err := s.agentClient.PairBrowserVM(ctx, host, bvm.ID, *machine.VMIP); err != nil {
    52				slog.Warn("heartbeat.browser_pairings.replay_pair_failed",
    53					"host_id", host.ID,
    54					"machine_id", machine.ID,
    55					"browser_vm_id", bvm.ID,
    56					"machine_vm_ip", *machine.VMIP,
    57					"browser_vm_ip", *bvm.VMIP,
    58					"error", err)
    59				continue
    60			}
    61	
    62			cdpTarget := fmt.Sprintf("%s:9222", *bvm.VMIP)
    63			if err := s.agentClient.SetCDPTarget(ctx, host, machine.ID, cdpTarget); err != nil {
    64				slog.Warn("heartbeat.browser_pairings.replay_cdp_target_failed",
    65					"host_id", host.ID,
    66					"machine_id", machine.ID,
    67					"browser_vm_id", bvm.ID,
    68					"target", cdpTarget,
    69					"error", err)
    70				continue
    71			}
    72	
    73			slog.Info("heartbeat.browser_pairings.replayed",
    74				"host_id", host.ID,
    75				"machine_id", machine.ID,
    76				"browser_vm_id", bvm.ID,
    77				"machine_vm_ip", *machine.VMIP,

    82	func (s *Server) ServiceTokenMiddleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
    83		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    84			if s.cfServiceTokenID == "" {
    85				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "service token not configured")
    86				return
    87			}
    88	
    89			clientID := r.Header.Get("CF-Access-Client-Id")
    90			clientSecret := r.Header.Get("CF-Access-Client-Secret")
    91	
    92			idMatch := subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(clientID), []byte(s.cfServiceTokenID)) == 1
    93			secMatch := subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(clientSecret), []byte(s.cfServiceTokenSec)) == 1
    94	
    95			if !idMatch || !secMatch {
    96				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "invalid service token")
    97				return
    98			}
    99			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
   100		})
   101	}

   103	func (s *Server) handleInternalResolve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
   104		var req struct {
   105			AccountSlug string `json:"account_slug"`
   106			MachineSlug string `json:"machine_slug"`
   107		}
   108		if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
   109			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid request body")
   110			return
   111		}
   112		if req.AccountSlug == "" || req.MachineSlug == "" {
   113			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "account_slug and machine_slug are required")
   114			return
   115		}
   116	
   117		route, err := s.store.ResolveRoute(r.Context(), req.AccountSlug, req.MachineSlug)
   118		if err != nil {
   119			writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "route not found")
   120			return
   121		}
   122	
   123		// Self-heal KV cache via RouteService (best-effort, already returning DB result)
   124		if s.routing != nil {
   125			if route.HostHostname != "" {
   126				_ = s.routing.SyncRouteToKV(r.Context(), routing.SyncKVRequest{
   127					AccountSlug:  req.AccountSlug,
   128					MachineSlug:  req.MachineSlug,
   129					MachineID:    route.MachineID,
   130					HostHostname: route.HostHostname,
   131					ProxyToken:   route.ProxyToken,
   132				})
   133			}
   134			_ = s.routing.SyncAccountToKV(r.Context(), req.AccountSlug, route.AccountID, route.UserIDs)
   135		}
   136	
   137		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, route)
   138	}

   140	// authenticateAgent validates the agent bearer token. It checks per-host token first
   141	// (if hostID is provided), then falls back to fleet-wide token.
   142	func (s *Server) authenticateAgent(ctx context.Context, r *http.Request, hostID int) (bool, error) {
   143		authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
   144		if !strings.HasPrefix(authHeader, "Bearer ") {
   145			return false, fmt.Errorf("missing bearer token")
   146		}
   147		token := strings.TrimPrefix(authHeader, "Bearer ")
   148	
   149		// Check per-host token first
   150		if hostID != 0 {
   151			host, err := s.store.GetHost(ctx, hostID)
   152			if err == nil && host.AgentToken != nil && *host.AgentToken != "" {
   153				if subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(token), []byte(*host.AgentToken)) == 1 {
   154					return true, nil
   155				}
   156				return false, fmt.Errorf("invalid agent token for host")
   157			}
   158		}
   159	
   160		// Fall back to fleet-wide token
   161		if s.agentToken == "" {
   162			return false, fmt.Errorf("agent token not configured")
   163		}
   164		if subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(token), []byte(s.agentToken)) != 1 {
   165			return false, fmt.Errorf("invalid agent token")
   166		}
   167		return true, nil
   168	}

   170	// handleAgentHeartbeat receives periodic heartbeats from host agents.
   171	// Auth: Bearer token must match FC_AGENT_TOKEN or per-host agent_token.
   172	func (s *Server) handleAgentHeartbeat(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {

   241		}

   246				slog.Warn("heartbeat.update_endpoint_failed", "host_id", hostID, "error", err)
   247			}
   248		}

    19	// authenticateAgentToken validates the bearer token against per-host or fleet-wide tokens.
    20	// Returns the host ID on success (0 for fleet-wide), or writes an error and returns false.
    21	func (s *Server) authenticateAgentToken(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (int, bool) {
    22		authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
    23		if !strings.HasPrefix(authHeader, "Bearer ") {
    24			writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "missing bearer token")
    25			return 0, false
    26		}
    27		token := strings.TrimPrefix(authHeader, "Bearer ")
    28	
    29		// Try per-host token lookup
    30		host, err := s.store.GetHostByAgentToken(r.Context(), token)
    31		if err == nil && host != nil {
    32			return host.ID, true
    33		}
    34	
    35		// Fall back to fleet-wide token
    36		if s.agentToken != "" && subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(token), []byte(s.agentToken)) == 1 {
    37			return 0, true
    38		}
    39	
    40		writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "invalid agent token")
    41		return 0, false
    42	}
    43	
    44	// validateMachinePlacement verifies that a machine is currently placed on the given host.
    45	// For fleet-wide tokens (hostID=0), the check is skipped.
    46	func (s *Server) validateMachinePlacement(ctx context.Context, machineID string, hostID int) error {
    47		if hostID == 0 {
    48			return nil
    49		}
    50		machine, err := s.store.GetMachine(ctx, machineID)
    51		if err != nil {
    52			return fmt.Errorf("machine not found")
    53		}
    54		if machine.HostID == nil || *machine.HostID != hostID {
    55			return fmt.Errorf("machine is not placed on this host")
    56		}
    57		return nil
    58	}

  9453	**CRITICAL**
  9454	- Deleted-VM history is not authorizable as designed. The doc says metrics outlive VM rows and deleted-VM history should still return, but ownership is checked from the live VM row. After hard delete, `machines` is gone, and metrics have no `account_id`, so the backend can either leak data or return 404. See [design](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:141), [deleted-history test](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:241), and hard delete in [postgres.go](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/store/postgres.go:604). Persist `account_id` on metrics at ingest, or create a VM tombstone/ownership table.
  9455	- Agent auth is underspecified and can become a write-any-VM hole if implemented with the existing helper. `authenticateAgentToken` accepts the fleet token and returns `hostID=0`; `validateMachinePlacement` then skips placement checks. The metrics endpoint must follow heartbeat auth: require integer `host_id`, authenticate token against that claimed host, and never let fleet-token auth bypass placement. See [design](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:111), [agent_auth.go](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/api/agent_auth.go:35), and heartbeat’s host-bound path in [agent_heartbeat.go](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/api/agent_heartbeat.go:140). Also the sample `host_id: "h-east-3"` conflicts with existing integer host IDs.
  9456	
  9457	**IMPORTANT**
  9458	- The schema contradicts the sampler contract: first sample has omitted CPU, but `cpu_pct REAL NOT NULL` cannot store it. Either do not insert first samples or make `cpu_pct` nullable. See [design](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:89) and [schema](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:124).
  9459	- Downsampling is not correct for late batches. The doc says `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and “worst-case error is one data point”, but the agent batches every 10s and backs off up to 60s. A partial minute can be frozen forever, losing 10-60 samples. Use a watermark/finalization delay, store `sample_count`, and make late reruns update the bucket deterministically. See [design](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:152) and [late-arrival claim](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:155).
  9460	- Daily partitions do not give exact 24h retention. Dropping whole daily partitions means `vm_metrics_1s` retains between 24h and almost 48h depending on UTC time. Either document that retention is daily-granular or use smaller partitions/row deletes. See [partition plan](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:143) and [drop policy](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:153).
  9461	- Maintenance jobs need singleton protection. Cloud Run/API mode already starts background loops per instance, so `EnsurePartitions`, `Downsample1s1m`, and `DropOldPartitions` need advisory locks or a real single scheduler. “Existing fleet scheduler” is not a concrete repo convention here. See API background loops in [cmd/server/main.go](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/cmd/server/main.go:334).
  9462	- The live SSE design scales with browsers, not VMs. `WHERE vm_id=$1 AND ts>$2` every second per open tab is not “cheap” just because indexed; 100 live tabs is 100 DB polls/sec plus long-lived Cloud Run handlers. Also agent batches every 10s, so “refreshing every second” will be bursty and up to 10s stale. See [live promise](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:14), [batching](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:33), and [polling claim](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:198).
  9463	- Routes do not match the codebase. The repo uses `/api`, not `/api/v1`, and user APIs are account-scoped under `/api/accounts/{accountId}`. Existing frontend API helpers also use `BASE="/api"`. Put metrics under `/api/accounts/{accountId}/machines/{id}/metrics` and `/browser-vms/{browserVmId}/metrics`. See [design route](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:164), [router](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/api/server.go:362), and [frontend API base](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/frontend/src/lib/api.ts:4).
  9464	- Schema needs tighter constraints/indexes. `kind TEXT` has no check constraint, `PRIMARY KEY (vm_id, ts)` ignores the discriminator, and `kind, ts` is not the endpoint access path. Use `CHECK (kind IN (...))`, persist `account_id`/`host_id`, and index `(account_id, kind, vm_id, ts)`.
  9465	- Ingest validation is missing. “Up to ~200 points” is only prose. Backend must enforce max batch size/body size, timestamp skew bounds, nonnegative memory, sane CPU bounds, duplicate semantics, and no future partitions created by malicious timestamps. See [wire format](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:95).
  9466	- Sampler needs reset behavior. If a cgroup disappears and later reappears with the same unit name, `cpu.stat` can reset while `prev` still contains old usage, producing negative CPU. Add pruning/reset tests around VM stop/start. See [discovery](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:67) and [prev map](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:82).
  9467	- Browser VM UI target is wrong. `BrowserVMLivePage` is a full-screen iframe proxy route, not a detail page with tabs. There is no `/browser-vms/:id` detail route today. See [design](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:204) and existing routes in [App.tsx](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/frontend/src/App.tsx:78).
  9468	
  9469	**MINOR**
  9470	- `CurrentFeature.md` still says the new tab is “Usage”, while the design correctly says “Resources”. Align it before implementation to avoid agents touching the existing billing `UsageTab`. See [design](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:17) and [CurrentFeature.md](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/CurrentFeature.md:11).

  9472	- If Recharts is added, call out the lockfile update and bundle impact. It is not currently in `frontend/package.json`.

     8	async function request<T>(path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<T> {
     9	  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    10	    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    11	    ...(init?.headers as Record<string, string>),
    12	  };
    13	  // ocm_token cookie is sent automatically via credentials: "include"
    14	  const res = await fetch(`${BASE}${path}`, {
    15	    ...init,
    16	    credentials: "include",
    17	    headers,
    18	  });
    19	  if (!res.ok) {
    20	    // Expired or invalid token — force logout immediately
    21	    if (res.status === 401 && !path.startsWith("/auth/")) {
    22	      window.location.href = "/signed-out";
    23	      throw new ApiError("Session expired", "unauthorized", 401, false);
    24	    }
    25	    const body = await res.json().catch(() => ({ error: res.statusText }));
    26	    throw new ApiError(
    27	      body.error || res.statusText,
    28	      body.code || "unknown",
    29	      res.status,
    30	      res.status === 429 || res.status >= 500,
    31	    );
    32	  }
    33	  if (res.status === 204) return undefined as T;
    34	  return res.json();
    35	}

   615			r.Patch("/traces/{traceID}", srv.handleOpikUpdateTrace)
   616	
   617			// Spans
   618			r.Post("/spans", srv.handleOpikCreateSpan)
   619			r.Post("/spans/batch", srv.handleOpikCreateSpansBatch)
   620			r.Patch("/spans/{spanID}", srv.handleOpikUpdateSpan)
   621	
   622			// Projects
   623			r.Get("/projects", srv.handleOpikListProjects)
   624			r.Post("/projects", srv.handleOpikCreateProject)
   625			r.Get("/projects/{projectID}", srv.handleOpikGetProject)
   626		})
   627	
   628		// Start tunnel reaper to clean up orphaned VM tunnels
   629		tunnel.StartReaper(ctx, tunnelMgr, s, 10*time.Minute)
   630	
   631		// Reconcile host capacity to match the current oversubscription ratio.
   632		// This ensures that if the ratio changes, existing hosts get updated.
   633		srv.reconcileHostCapacity(ctx)
   634	
   635		srv.router = r
   636		return srv
   637	}

   683	// reconcileHostCapacity recalculates capacity_vcpus for all active hosts
   684	// based on their physical CPU count (from capabilities) and the current
   685	// oversubscription ratio. This ensures that changing VCPU_OVERSUBSCRIPTION_RATIO
   686	// takes effect on existing hosts at startup, not only on newly created ones.
   687	func (s *Server) reconcileHostCapacity(ctx context.Context) {
   688		updated, err := s.store.ReconcileHostCapacityVCPUs(ctx, s.vcpuOversubRatio)
   689		if err != nil {
   690			slog.Error("reconcile_host_capacity.failed", "error", err)
   691			return
   692		}
   693		if updated > 0 {
   694			slog.Info("reconcile_host_capacity.updated", "hosts_updated", updated, "ratio", s.vcpuOversubRatio)
   695		}
   696	}

   698	func slogRequestLogger(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
   699		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
   700			start := time.Now()
   701			ww := middleware.NewWrapResponseWriter(w, r.ProtoMajor)
   702			next.ServeHTTP(ww, r)
   703			slog.Info("http.request",
   704				"method", r.Method,
   705				"path", r.URL.Path,
   706				"status", ww.Status(),
   707				"duration_ms", time.Since(start).Milliseconds(),
   708				"request_id", middleware.GetReqID(r.Context()),
   709				"trace_id", ww.Header().Get("X-Trace-ID"),
   710			)
   711		})
   712	}

   714	func traceIDMiddleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
   715		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
   716			traceID := r.Header.Get("X-Trace-ID")
   717			if traceID == "" {
   718				traceID = tracing.GenerateTraceID()
   719			}
   720			ctx := tracing.WithTraceID(r.Context(), traceID)
   721			w.Header().Set("X-Trace-ID", traceID)
   722			next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
   723		})
   724	}

   739	// ---- Middleware ----
   740	
   741	type contextKey string
   742	
   743	const (
   744		accountMemberKey contextKey = "accountMember"
   745		accountIDKey     contextKey = "accountID"
   746	)
   747	
   748	func (s *Server) AccountMiddleware(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
   749		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
   750			accountID, err := parseIntParam(r, "accountId")
   751			if err != nil {
   752				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid account id")
   753				return
   754			}
   755	
   756			claims := auth.UserFromContext(r.Context())
   757			if claims == nil {
   758				writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized")
   759				return
   760			}
   761	
   762			member, err := s.store.GetAccountMember(r.Context(), accountID, claims.UserID)
   763			if err != nil {
   764				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "access denied to this account")
   765				return
   766			}
   767	
   768			ctx := context.WithValue(r.Context(), accountMemberKey, member)
   769			ctx = context.WithValue(ctx, accountIDKey, accountID)
   770			next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(ctx))
   771		})
   772	}
   773	
   774	// requireSuperuser blocks requests from non-superuser accounts.
   775	func (s *Server) requireSuperuser(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
   776		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
   777			if !isSuperuser(r.Context()) {
   778				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "admin access required")
   779				return
   780			}
   781			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
   782		})
   783	}
   784	
   785	// isSuperuser reports whether the current request is authenticated as the
   786	// superuser. Used by handlers that need to gate individual fields (e.g.
   787	// tenant-supplied host_id/region placement pinning) rather than whole
   788	// routes.
   789	func isSuperuser(ctx context.Context) bool {
   790		claims := auth.UserFromContext(ctx)
   791		return claims != nil && claims.Email == "mathewma@gmail.com"
   792	}

   794	// accountIDFromContext returns the account ID set by AccountMiddleware.
   795	func accountIDFromContext(ctx context.Context) int {
   796		id, _ := ctx.Value(accountIDKey).(int)
   797		return id
   798	}
   799	
   800	// userIDFromContext returns a pointer to the authenticated user's ID, or nil if not available.
   801	func userIDFromContext(ctx context.Context) *int {
   802		claims := auth.UserFromContext(ctx)
   803		if claims == nil || claims.UserID == 0 {
   804			return nil
   805		}
   806		return &claims.UserID
   807	}

   809	// accountMemberFromContext returns the account member set by AccountMiddleware.
   810	func accountMemberFromContext(ctx context.Context) *store.AccountMember {
   811		m, _ := ctx.Value(accountMemberKey).(*store.AccountMember)
   812		return m
   813	}
   814	
   815	// requireOwnerRole checks that the current account member has the "owner" role.
   816	// Returns true if access is denied (and the response has been written).
   817	func requireOwnerRole(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) bool {
   818		member := accountMemberFromContext(r.Context())
   819		if member == nil || member.Role != "owner" {
   820			writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "owner role required for this action")
   821			return true
   822		}
   823		return false
   824	}
   825	
   826	// requireRole returns middleware that checks the account member has one of the allowed roles.
   827	func requireRole(roles ...string) func(http.Handler) http.Handler {
   828		allowed := make(map[string]bool, len(roles))
   829		for _, r := range roles {
   830			allowed[r] = true
   831		}
   832		return func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
   833			return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
   834				member := accountMemberFromContext(r.Context())
   835				if member == nil || !allowed[member.Role] {
   836					writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "insufficient permissions")
   837					return
   838				}
   839				next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
   840			})

   577	// ListRunningRoutes returns route data for all running machines with valid hosts.
   578	func (s *PostgresStore) ListRunningRoutes(ctx context.Context) ([]RouteData, error) {
   579		rows, err := s.pool.Query(ctx, `
   580			SELECT a.slug, m.id, m.slug, h.tunnel_url, m.proxy_token
   581			FROM machines m
   582			JOIN accounts a ON m.account_id = a.id
   583			JOIN hosts h ON m.host_id = h.id
   584			WHERE m.status = 'running'
   585			  AND m.proxy_token IS NOT NULL
   586			  AND h.tunnel_url IS NOT NULL
   587		`)
   588		if err != nil {
   589			return nil, err
   590		}
   591		defer rows.Close()
   592	
   593		var routes []RouteData
   594		for rows.Next() {
   595			var r RouteData
   596			if err := rows.Scan(&r.AccountSlug, &r.MachineID, &r.MachineSlug, &r.HostHostname, &r.ProxyToken); err != nil {
   597				return nil, err
   598			}
   599			routes = append(routes, r)
   600		}
   601		return routes, rows.Err()
   602	}

     1	-- browser_vms table
     2	--
     3	-- ON DELETE semantics:
     4	--   - account_id: CASCADE so deleting an account drops its browser VM records
     5	--     instead of blocking the account teardown on dangling rows.
     6	--   - host_id: SET NULL so retiring a host clears the pointer rather than
     7	--     blocking host decommissioning. The agent-side VM is already gone at
     8	--     that point; the DB just needs to stop pointing at the missing host.
     9	CREATE TABLE browser_vms (
    10	    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    11	    account_id      INT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    12	    slug            TEXT NOT NULL,
    13	    name            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    14	    host_id         INT REFERENCES hosts(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
    15	    vm_ip           TEXT,
    16	    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'stopped',
    17	    vcpus           INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    18	    memory_mb       INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1024,
    19	    cdp_port        INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 9222,
    20	    rootfs_version  TEXT,
    21	    error_message   TEXT,
    22	    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    23	    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    24	    CONSTRAINT browser_vms_status_check CHECK (status IN ('stopped', 'provisioning', 'running', 'error')),
    25	    UNIQUE(account_id, slug)
    26	);
    27	
    28	CREATE INDEX idx_browser_vms_account ON browser_vms(account_id);
    29	CREATE INDEX idx_browser_vms_host ON browser_vms(host_id) WHERE host_id IS NOT NULL;
    30	
    31	-- browser_vm_placements table
    32	--
    33	-- host_id CASCADE: placements are ephemeral capacity accounting, so
    34	-- decommissioning a host should drop their placement history rather than
    35	-- block the host deletion. browser_vm_id is already CASCADE for the same
    36	-- reason — the placement has no meaning without its owning browser VM.
    37	CREATE TABLE browser_vm_placements (
    38	    id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    39	    browser_vm_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES browser_vms(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    40	    host_id         INT NOT NULL REFERENCES hosts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    41	    vm_ip           TEXT,
    42	    state           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'reserved',
    43	    reserved_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    44	    activated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    45	    released_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,
    46	    CONSTRAINT browser_vm_placements_state_check CHECK (state IN ('reserved', 'active', 'released'))
    47	);
    48	
    49	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_bvp_active_browser_vm
    50	ON browser_vm_placements(browser_vm_id) WHERE released_at IS NULL;
    51	
    52	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_bvp_active_host_ip
    53	ON browser_vm_placements(host_id, vm_ip) WHERE released_at IS NULL;
    54	
    55	CREATE INDEX idx_bvp_host
    56	ON browser_vm_placements(host_id) WHERE released_at IS NULL;
    57	
    58	-- pairing column on machines
    59	--
    60	-- ON DELETE SET NULL: deleting a browser VM must not be blocked by a stale
    61	-- pairing pointer on a machine row. handleDeleteBrowserVM runs the agent-side
    62	-- unpair first (best effort), and this constraint guarantees the DB delete
    63	-- succeeds even if the agent unpair failed and left the pointer in place.
    64	ALTER TABLE machines ADD COLUMN browser_vm_id UUID REFERENCES browser_vms(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
    65	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_machines_browser_vm ON machines(browser_vm_id) WHERE browser_vm_id IS NOT NULL;

    16	func (s *Server) handleProvisionHost(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    17		if s.provisioner == nil {
    18			writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "provisioner not configured")
    19			return
    20		}
    21	
    22		var req struct {
    23			MachineType string `json:"machine_type"`
    24			Zone        string `json:"zone"`
    25		}
    26		if r.Body != nil {
    27			_ = json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
    28		}
    29	
    30		// Machine type presets (must support KVM / nested virtualization).
    31		// vCPU capacity = physical CPU threads * oversubscription ratio.
    32		// The ratio is read from VCPU_OVERSUBSCRIPTION_RATIO (default 2, max 3).
    33		type preset struct {
    34			physicalCPUs int
    35			memoryMB     int
    36		}
    37		validTypes := map[string]preset{
    38			"n2-standard-2": {2, 8192},
    39			"n2-standard-4": {4, 16384},
    40			"n2-standard-8": {8, 32768},
    41			"c2-standard-4": {4, 16384},
    42		}
    43	
    44		if req.MachineType == "" {
    45			req.MachineType = "n2-standard-2"
    46		}
    47		p, ok := validTypes[req.MachineType]
    48		if !ok {
    49			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid machine_type: must be one of n2-standard-2, n2-standard-4, n2-standard-8, c2-standard-4")
    50			return
    51		}
    52	
    53		machineType := req.MachineType
    54		physicalCPUs := p.physicalCPUs
    55		vcpus := physicalCPUs * s.vcpuOversubRatio
    56		memoryMB := p.memoryMB
    57	
    58		go func() {
    59			ctx := context.Background()
    60			host, err := s.provisioner.ProvisionHost(ctx, machineType, physicalCPUs, vcpus, memoryMB, req.Zone)
    61			if err != nil {
    62				slog.Error("host.provision.failed", "error", err)
    63				return
    64			}
    65			slog.Info("host.provision.completed", "host_id", host.ID, "host_name", host.VMName)
    66		}()
    67	
    68		writeJSON(w, http.StatusAccepted, map[string]string{
    69			"status":  "provisioning",
    70			"message": "Host provisioning started in background",
    71		})
    72	}

**New Findings**
- CRITICAL: Per-host-only metrics auth will reject current GCE-provisioned hosts. Rev. 2 says “Hosts always have a per-host token” at [design:123](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:123), but provisioned hosts are created without `agent_token` and GCE metadata passes the fleet token. See [postgres.go:688](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/store/postgres.go:688), [provisioner.go:210](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/provisioner/provisioner.go:210). You need to generate/store/pass a per-host token for provisioned hosts and plan rotation for existing hosts.

- IMPORTANT: Advisory lock key encoding itself is fine for Postgres `bigint`; `0x564D5F455053` fits signed int64. The broken part is the acquire/release shape at [design:201](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:201). With `pgxpool`, `AcquireAdvisory` and `ReleaseAdvisory` can run on different sessions. Use `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` inside a transaction that runs the job, or hold a dedicated `pgxpool.Conn`.

- IMPORTANT: The ingest placement SQL references a nonexistent `deleted_at` column: [design:130](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:130). The `machines` schema has no `deleted_at` at [001_initial.sql:80](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/migrations/001_initial.sql:80), and delete is hard delete at [postgres.go:604](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/store/postgres.go:604).

- IMPORTANT: 1 Hz polling still preserves the prior “100 tabs = 100 DB reads/s” problem and now adds full-window response churn. Since agents POST every 10 seconds, [design:269](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:269) should poll every 5-10 seconds or fetch only `ts > lastSeen`, while the chart can still animate locally.

**New Findings**
- CRITICAL: Per-host-only metrics auth will reject current GCE-provisioned hosts. Rev. 2 says “Hosts always have a per-host token” at [design:123](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:123), but provisioned hosts are created without `agent_token` and GCE metadata passes the fleet token. See [postgres.go:688](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/store/postgres.go:688), [provisioner.go:210](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/provisioner/provisioner.go:210). You need to generate/store/pass a per-host token for provisioned hosts and plan rotation for existing hosts.

- IMPORTANT: Advisory lock key encoding itself is fine for Postgres `bigint`; `0x564D5F455053` fits signed int64. The broken part is the acquire/release shape at [design:201](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:201). With `pgxpool`, `AcquireAdvisory` and `ReleaseAdvisory` can run on different sessions. Use `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` inside a transaction that runs the job, or hold a dedicated `pgxpool.Conn`.

- IMPORTANT: The ingest placement SQL references a nonexistent `deleted_at` column: [design:130](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:130). The `machines` schema has no `deleted_at` at [001_initial.sql:80](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/migrations/001_initial.sql:80), and delete is hard delete at [postgres.go:604](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/backend/internal/store/postgres.go:604).

- IMPORTANT: 1 Hz polling still preserves the prior “100 tabs = 100 DB reads/s” problem and now adds full-window response churn. Since agents POST every 10 seconds, [design:269](/home/mantiz/OpenClawMachines/docs/plans/2026-04-29-vm-instrumentation-design.md:269) should poll every 5-10 seconds or fetch only `ts > lastSeen`, while the chart can still animate locally.
